findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There are Parmesan cheese shakers observed to be stored on tables for consumer use. According to the PIC in the kitchen, these shakers are put in the cooler every night and then placed on the tables every day for consumer use. The cheese is imported grated pecorino Romano cheese from Casale and the box is stored in the walk-in cooler and states to “KEEP REFRIGERATED”. The facility can either cease this practice and store the Parmesan cheese shakers in a cooler and remove them only when a consumer wants to use them OR can reach out to the manufacturer to determine if the Parmesan cheese only needs to be refrigerated for QUALITY and not SAFETY. A follow up is scheduled for 8/5/2026 to allow time for the facility to decide and to reach out to the manufacturer. Ensure that proof is provided if reaching out to the manufacturer. If there are any questions, please reach out to the inspector.

2-301.12: Observed an employee wash his hands for only a few seconds and did not use a barrier when Turning off the faucet after washing his hands. Ensure employees properly wash their hands. Also, employees were observed cleaning and then went to prep food without washing their hands. Ensure employees wash their hands when changing tasks and before food prep. Proper hand washing education was provided.  

(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed two soda nozzles at the bar to be soiled with mildew and other debris. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned frequently so they are maintained clean to sight and touch. Manager stated he would clean these surfaces during the inspection. 
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Observed wet wiping cloths to not be stored inside sanitizer between uses. Wiping cloths were observed on counters, inside a hand sink, and on prep tables. Ensure wiping cloths are properly stored inside sanitizer. 
(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed the area behind the soda nozzles in the wait area to be soiled. Ensure the area behind the soda nozzle is cleaned frequently so it is maintained clean. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed a dirty spatula to be stored on the magnetic strip used to store knives. Ensure only clean knives are stored on the magnetic strip. The spatula was pulled to be cleaned, and the magnetic strip was wiped down. Also, clean knives in the wait station were observed being stored inside a container with food particles inside the container. Server stated the container would be changed. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer was measured at 100ppm in the kitchen sani bucket. Ensure quat sanitizer concentration maintains a concentration between 200 and 400ppm. Sani bucket changed during inspection. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Observed clean spoons in the wait area to be stored with the handle down. Spoons and other utensils must be stored with the handle facing upward. 

Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D).

Reference 6-305.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed pasta from the weekend and sauce that was pulled from the freezer over the weekend to no be properly date marked. Additionally, milk, orange juice, and to go salads were not date marked in the wait area cooler and at the bar. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Pasta was discarded, and the remaining foods were labeled with the date it was pulled from the freezer. Reference 3-501.17.

Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Thermometers were placed in the coolers during inspection, Reference 4-204-112.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15  (C) The exterior door seal in the kitchen has a gap in it that allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on milk in wait station serving area fridge. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.
